messages:
jessica: Heads-up — ran a targeted bring-up for the new L32 model on h100/eu-west and saw weird p95 spikes when the kernel selector flipped to flashv3 for small payloads. Figured we should sketch a safety net before a rollout.
omar: Can you paste the perf snippets? small payloads as in <=64 tokens?
jessica: Yep <=64. Here's the tail I saw in prod-sim: 
```
model=L32 | hw=h100-eu | kernel=flashv3 | batch=4 | seq=64
p50=18ms p95=220ms p99=520ms
-- preceding kernel=triton-sparse --
p50=20ms p95=58ms p99=120ms
```
liam: Whoa p95 went up 4x after switch. Is KV warmup contributing?
sana: Do we have the request shape distribution? flashv3 tends to suffer with high microburst/noisy queueing for small batches.
jessica: Distribution skewed: 70% <=32 tokens, 25% 33-128, 5% >128. We expected flashv3 to win overall but the tail is killer for SLO.
tia: Possible causes: kernel packing heuristics + extra kernel prep on cold instances. Also q8 quant path changes allocate different temp buffers.
omar: Did we compare on h100 vs a100? vendor libcudnn/triton might be better at tiny-batch latency.
jessica: Quick cross-region numbers: 
- h100-eu-west (flashv3): p95 220ms
- h100-eu-west (triton): p95 58ms
- a100-us-west (flashv3): p95 85ms
- a100-us-west (triton): p95 92ms
So it's region+hw combo.
liam: That suggests the flashv3 build we use in eu region might have a different kernel tuning (maybe compiler flags) or driver mismatch.
sana: We should avoid blanket kernel switchover policy. Propose: 1) per-region per-hardware signal, 2) include payload-shape histogram gating, 3) canary with traffic split and an automatic fallback if p95 > baseline*2 within 15min.
jessica: Agreed. Also want a preflight perf job during model onboarding that runs microbenchmarks with small-batch hotpaths and q8 variants. Add a "safety margin" metric.
tia: For rollout config, suggestion: {"switch_window": "off-peak 2h", "min_samples": 5000, "p95_threshold_multiplier": 1.8, "grace_period": 900} — where grace_period is seconds.
omar: Add a KV-cache priming step for flashv3 builds: run 100 warmup requests with seq=32 to populate temp allocs. See if p95 stabilizes.
eng-bot: perf-alert: triggered test run 1735342400; p95 exceeded threshold in eu-west flashv3 on h100 (220ms) — auto-rollout paused. :warning:
liam: Good — rollout pause worked. Next steps: run a targeted repro on dedicated eu-west h100 with profiling and nvprof traces, check kernel versions (flashv3 rev + triton plugin).
sana: I'll draft the playbook entry for eng-runtime: gating rules + suggested thresholds + warmup job template. Can someone add the microbench to onboarding CI?
jessica: I'll add tests to onboarding CI and include the warmup step. Omar, can you take the profiling traces?
omar: On it. Will drop a short summary here when I have the nvprof captures.
sana: tl;dr for PMs: we won't do global kernel flips automatically; we'll use region/hw/payload gating + warmup + canary + auto-fallback. That should keep user-facing latency from regressing. :thumbsup:
